language.note: Nicaragua's census does not ask the population's language. The 2005 census's only language question (P08, "¿Habla la lengua o idioma del pueblo indígena o comunidad étnica a la que pertenece?") was put only to the members of the seven Caribbean-coast peoples and communities -- Rama, Garífuna, Mayangna, Miskitu, Ulwa, Creole and the coast's mestizos, whose 270,870 people are exactly its answers -- and asks whether they speak their people's language, not what anybody speaks. It is not a composition, and the rest of the country was not asked.
